differences.what: massing: the light stone front against the brick north flank, two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard, the rear range lower behind the flank
differences.how: T-3163's camera (5.5 px RMS on ten readings) lands the render's corners and cornice on the vignette's

differences.what: the pavilion: forward of the front, flush with the south wall, one window to a storey in a stone surround

the pavilion's crown: a pedimented attic front with its paired lights and finial standing between the slated cheeks of a steep crown; the build carries the pavilion's stone up a full-width attic under a coped gable, so its cheeks are stone where the vignette's are slate
the pavilion's paired attic lights under the pediment, and the finial
differences.how: T-3163: the attic storey's two lights on a mullion under the coped gable and its finial

differences.what: the triple window group on both storeys, the door north of the pavilion with a window over it
differences.how: T-3163's places through the engraving's camera, which land on the vignette's within about 5 px

differences.what: the moulded heads over the front's windows
the mansard's cresting along the curb
differences.how: T-3163: K10's iron cresting round the deck

differences.what: the triple group's dormer: drawn broad with paired lights between scrolled consoles under a pediment that rises over the curb; the build's is K05's 2.0 m gabled dormer stopping under it
the small dormer over the door, and the north flank's dormers
the hooded window on the north flank
differences.how: T-3163: the box bay under its hood

differences.what: the stoop climbing from the north to the landing
the stoop's iron rail on the landing and flight: the build's cheek is K07's stone
differences.how: the Chicagology engraving draws stone cheeks there; two pictures disagree

differences.what: the arched opening under the landing: not built
differences.how: T-1894: the round-arched doorway in the landing's street face, built to the Chicagology engraving's camera; with the landing drawn to its length (fourth revision) it is 1.25 m across at v 5.8 m, a little south of the face's middle as this vignette puts it (the render's arch lands on the vignette's within about 1 px), its crown about 1.13 m up. The vignette draws it broader still, about 22 px against the render's 13 px, where the engraving, after a photograph and four times this plate's scale, draws it about 1.25 m; at this plate's half-metre scale the two pictures do not agree on its width (the engraving's record)

differences.what: the stack at the flank's rear corner, over the rear range: T-1894 stands it on the range's deck (u -4.8 m, 16.6 m high, through the engraving's camera); the vignette draws it in the same place
a third tall stack on the flank between the two the build stands
differences.how: the Chicagology engraving draws no stack there; two pictures disagree

differences.what: the stone's and brick's colours: the vignette is a monochrome print
the south flank and the rear
the walk, the trees and the figures
the low line before the house and the post at the walk
differences.how: T-3206 lays a 0.3 m stone coping on the street line with 0.75 m posts either side of the side-stoop walk's opening (the album's post at about s 1.4) and the K14 walk from the side stoop's foot

differences.what: the dormers' paired casements: only the first light of each pair was cut through the dormer's face, the second standing glazed behind it
differences.how: T-3297: each of K06's lights is cut through the face now (k01_frontage.round_dormer_body), so both lights of each pair open as the picture draws them

differences.what: the landing's length: the vignette's landing face runs from the flight's head to the pavilion, about 2.5 m at 13 px a metre, the build's 1.8 m; the Chicagology engraving draws the same, and its record says how
differences.how: T-1894 (fourth revision): the landing runs v 4.4-7.1 m, 2.7 m from the flight's head to the pavilion, and stands at the door's 1.7 m floor (entrance_floor_m) a few risers under the hall, so its top edge, its north end and the flight's foot land on the vignette's within about 1-2 px (half a metre or less at this plate's scale)

differences.what: the north flank's box bay: drawn on a corbelled block under its broad hooded light with a basement light beneath it in the flank's wall; the build carried it to grade with the light in its foot
differences.how: T-1894: K08's corbelled oriel on the principal floor, its foot at 1.75 m, and the basement light in the wall under it, as the Chicagology engraving's record measures them; the vignette's half-metre scale agrees

differences.what: the flank's basement lights under its window columns, which the vignette draws square-headed
differences.how: T-1894: all five the Chicagology engraving draws are laid square-headed in the brick, 0.45-1.45 m over grade: under the 2.15 m and 11.0 m columns and the box bay (PR #2073), and now under the 0.25 m column (K01 lets a read light stand 0.1 m inside a flank's rear end where a rear wing carries the wall on flush) and under the rear range's flank column (a wing's basement lights may be square-headed); the vignette's small square lights along the flank's foot agree

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
